Operator: Good day, and welcome to the NexusGuard Cybersecurity Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. During the Q&A session, please press star then one on your touchtone phone if you would like to ask a question. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NexusGuard's results for the Q3 2024. With me on today's call are Sarah Chen, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Harlan, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Lena Voss, Chief Technology Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Security Officer; Jordan Lee, VP of Sales; Emily Torres, Chief Marketing Officer; and Kyle Bennett, Chief Product Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen: Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. NexusGuard delivered exceptional results in the Q3, exceeding expectations across all key metrics. Our performance reflects the strength of our product portfolio, our expanding customer base, and our commitment to innovation. The adoption rate of our Falcon XDR platform is accelerating, demonstrating its power in providing unified threat detection across endpoints, networks, and cloud environments, and the unmatched value we bring to our customers in combating sophisticated attacks.

Our strategic priorities are focused on eight key areas: driving expansion within our existing large accounts, acquiring significant numbers of new customers, maintaining low churn through proactive retention, enhancing the effectiveness of our go-to-market strategy, rolling out impactful recent product and feature launches, gaining market share across core segments, closely monitoring and responding to the evolving threat landscape, and providing clear next quarter billings guidance.

These priorities are yielding results in a cybersecurity market under immense pressure from rising threats and regulatory demands. Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Harlan to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Mike Harlan: Thank you, Sarah. We achieved record revenue of $1.42 billion in the Q3, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. Our gross margin remained strong at 82%, and we continued to invest in growth initiatives. Operating expenses were $950 million. Net income was $280 million, resulting in earnings per share of $0.85. We are increasing our full-year revenue and earnings guidance based on our strong performance to date.

Before diving deeper, let me unpack one of our strongest growth drivers this quarter: expansion within our existing large accounts. We define large accounts as those generating over $1 million in annual recurring revenue, or ARR, which currently represents about 65% of our total ARR base, or roughly $2.8 billion out of our $4.3 billion total ARR as of quarter-end. In Q3, expansion revenue from these large accounts hit a record $178 million, up 28% year-over-year and 12% quarter-over-quarter. This contributed to our overall dollar-based net retention rate, or NRR, climbing to 128%—our highest in three years and well ahead of the cybersecurity industry average of around 115% as reported by peers.

For every $100 of ARR we had from these accounts at the start of last year, we're now retaining $128, with the incremental $28 coming purely from upsells, cross-sells, and usage-based growth. Excluding any contraction drag—which was minimal at just 2% this quarter—our gross retention held steady at 98%, underscoring the stickiness of our platform. Driving this is our land-and-expand model, fueled by the shift toward consolidated, AI-native security platforms. Customers face escalating threats—ransomware attacks surged 37% YoY per our Threat Intelligence Report, with groups like LockBit 3.0 and BlackCat targeting cloud-native environments. Board-level mandates for Zero Trust Architecture are accelerating, with 72% of our large accounts citing regulatory compliance—like NIS2 in Europe or SEC cyber disclosure rules in the U.S.—as a top trigger.

Our flagship upsell path is from core Endpoint Detection and Response, or EDR, via NexusGuard Falcon, to our full Extended Detection and Response, or XDR, stack, integrating identity threat detection from our Falcon Identity Protection acquisition. In Q3, 41% of expansions involved XDR modules, adding an average of $450,000 in net new ARR per account. This features agentless deployment via eBPF for sub-millisecond latency in Kubernetes environments, resonating with hyperscale customers.

Cloud security accounted for 35% of expansion dollars. With public cloud spend projected to hit $700 billion globally in 2024 per Gartner, customers are adopting our Cloud-Native Application Protection Platform, or CNAPP, combining Cloud Workload Protection, or CWP, with Infrastructure as Code scanning. Traction in serverless workloads on AWS Lambda and Azure Functions comes from runtime behavioral analytics detecting cryptojacking and data exfiltration in real-time, driving a 32% YoY increase in cloud security ARR from large accounts, with average expansions of 22% as enterprises consolidate from point solutions.

Usage-based growth contributed 18%, with our Secure Access Service Edge, or SASE, fabric—powered by our global 200+ PoP network—seeing SWG and ZTNA traffic volumes spike 45% YoY amid remote/hybrid work. Pricing is metered on encrypted throughput, so scaling to 100 Gbps+ per site accretes revenue naturally. We've layered in our GenAI Security module for prompt injection and model poisoning in tools like ChatGPT Enterprise—early adopters like a top-5 financial institution expanded by 150%.

Regionally, North America delivered 62% of expansion revenue at $110 million, up 25% YoY, with hyperscalers and F500 firms deepening stacks post breaches like Change Healthcare. EMEA jumped 42% to $42 million, driven by GDPR fines totaling €2.7 billion in 2023 and NIS2 deadlines—German DAX 40 companies averaged 28% expansion with our Data Loss Prevention, or DLP, for SaaS apps like Microsoft 365. APAC grew fastest at 55% YoY to $26 million, with Singapore's PDPA and Australia's CDR pushing financial services; we landed a $15 million upsell with a major APAC telco for 5G edge security.

This stems from our Account Team Playbook 2.0, emphasizing platform velocity and targeting 3x multi-product adoption, now at 68% versus 52% last year. Professional services generated $65 million—up 35%—via red-team simulations. Partnerships like AWS Marketplace drove 22% of expansions, while ServiceNow integrations reduced TCO by 30%.

Looking ahead, IDC forecasts 13.8% cybersecurity CAGR through 2027, but our expansions should outpace at 20%+ as consolidation accelerates—McKinsey notes 70% of CISOs reducing vendors from 50 to 10. Cyber remains recession-proof, even as IT budgets flatline.

Risks include elongated EMEA sales cycles at 7 months versus 5, and potential SMB spillover, mitigated by our Customer Success AI flagging at-risk accounts 45 days early for 95% renewals. This moat de-risks growth, drives margins to 82%, and positions us for $6 billion ARR by FY26.

On new customer acquisition, in Q3 we added 452 new customers, a 38% year-over-year increase from 327 in Q3 2023 and 14% sequential from Q1's 397. This tracks to full-year guidance of 1,800 to 2,000 new customers, at least 35% YoY growth. Enterprise—ACV over $100K—drove 128 new, up 42% YoY, including 17 Fortune 500 like a U.S. financial migrating to our Next-Gen EDR and a European OEM for ZTNA post-SolarWinds. Mid-market/SMB added 248, up 36%, via self-service onboarding. Public sector gained 76, with CISA Zero Trust conversions.

North America took 62% (280 customers), boosted by ransomware like Clop's MOVEit exploits pushing MDR. EMEA added 108 (24%), up 45% with Paris data center and NIS2. APAC 64 (14%), accelerating via Tokyo expansion and AWS/Alibaba partnerships against APT41.

Powering this: Q2 ShieldAI Guardian launch with 65% enterprise adoption for sub-5-minute MTTD. Channel partnerships generated 22% wins. Net dollar retention at 118%, RPO up 40% YoY. Tailwinds: Log4Shell effects, 300% ransomware-as-a-service rise, SEC rules. Q4 expects 480-520 adds, APAC to 18%.

Customer retention shines: logo churn at 2.8%, down 12.5% YoY from 3.2%, 10th straight improvement. Annualized at 11% TTM, below 15-18% industry. NRR 118%. Reasons: M&A 38% (e.g., bank/healthcare consolidations), retained 65% revenue; budget 26% (EMEA uptick); competitive 20% (CrowdStrike/SentinelOne, but won back 15%); fit/support 10%; involuntary 6%.

North America 2.4%, APAC 3.4%, EMEA 3.2%. Countering with Retention Engine AI reducing voluntary churn 22%, multi-year contracts at 68%, tiered CSMs yielding 140% NRR for whales. Q4 churn 2.5-2.7%, expansions 72% via CSPM.

Market share trends: overall 4.2%, up 55 bps YoY in $215B TAM (IDC 13.8% CAGR). EDR 14.8% in $18B (from 12.1%), FalconX 7.2 GenAI cutting MTTR 65%, 60% Defender win rates. NGFW 7.5% in $42B, 22% SASE submarket. CNAPP 11.2% in $25B (doubled), Nebula blocking 2.3M LockBit. NA 6.8%, APAC 3.9%, EMEA 4.1%. Pillars: 22% R&D, ecosystem, $450M ThreatGuard M&A.

Recent launches drove 28% revenue, $5.8B ARR up 35%. Sentinel AI XDR: 78% MTTD cut, 1,200 customers, $180M ARR. ZeroTrust Edge 2.0 SASE with PQC: 850% ramp, $120M. Ransomware Shield Pro: 650 customers, $95M, sub-1-hour recovery. Total 55% bookings, RPO $7.2B up 41%, NPS 68, churn 3.2%.

Next quarter billings guidance: $1.42B-$1.46B, 8-11% sequential from $1.31B, 28-32% YoY, mid-30% FY. Subscriptions $1.31B-$1.35B, NRR 116-119%. New logo ACV 22-25% YoY, pipeline +35%. NA 65% (10-13%), EMEA 18%, APAC 12% 40% YoY. Megatrends: AI threats, consolidation, regs. Visibility from $4.2B RPO 1.8x guide.

Dr. Lena Voss: Thank you, Mike. Our technology team is focused on developing cutting-edge security solutions leveraging AI, machine learning, and cloud computing. Key areas include advancing our XDR and CNAPP innovations to counter AI-augmented threats like polymorphic malware and deepfakes, where we've seen 150% spikes in phishing kits.

Raj Patel: Security remains our top priority. We're continuously monitoring the threat landscape—global incidents up 37% YoY to 2,800 attacks weekly per our report, ransomware 42% with $1.8M demands. Cloud misconfigs 31%, ICS 40%. NA compliance-heavy, EMEA NIS2 surge, APAC APTs. Our Nexus XDR cuts dwell time to 4 minutes, PQC rollout addresses harvest-now-decrypt-later.

Jordan Lee: We're seeing strong demand across geographies and verticals. Our sales team builds relationships and expands share via land-and-expand, channels now 58% bookings up from 42%. AWS/Microsoft/Google alliances 3x co-sell pipeline, partner ARR +62%. CAC payback 11.2 months, inbound 65%. High-ACV $1.4M avg, 112 $1M+ deals. NA +52%, EMEA +61% NIS2, APAC +39%. ShieldXDR 2.0 shortens cycles 28%, FY24 45-50% ARR target.

Emily Torres: Our marketing efforts build brand awareness and demand via digital, PR, events, and thought leadership positioning NexusGuard as a trusted advisor.

Kyle Bennett: Our product strategy delivers integrated solutions addressing evolving needs, gathering feedback to exceed expectations. Sentinel AI, ZeroTrust Edge, Ransomware Shield are accelerating multi-product adoption to 68%.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Instructions for the Q&A session. First question comes from David Kim with Morgan Stanley.

David Kim: Congrats on the quarter. Can you quantify XDR attach rates and expansions?

Sarah Chen: Thanks, David. In large accounts, 41% of expansions involved XDR, adding $450K ARR avg. Overall, 62% of new EDR logos expand to XDR within 12 months, adding 18 points to NRR, driven by agentless eBPF advantages.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Chen with Goldman Sachs.

Lisa Chen: On billings guidance, any color on risks if rates stay high?

Mike Harlan: Solid question. Macro could pressure low end with elongated decisions, but 95% NRR and $4.2B RPO give 1.8x visibility. Agentless pivot mitigates hardware issues. Confident in mid-30% FY growth.

Operator: Next question comes from Raj Singh with JPMorgan.

Raj Singh: Thoughts on threat landscape evolution impacting products?

Dr. Lena Voss: Threats are AI-augmented—150% phishing spike, supply chain +55%. Our Sentinel AI with graph neural networks detects 45% faster, blocking 2.7M cloud risks. PQC in all products future-proofs.

Operator: Next question comes from Maria Lopez with Barclays.

Maria Lopez: Churn details and mitigation?

Raj Patel: Logo churn 2.8%, NRR 118%. M&A 38%, budget 26%, competitive 20%. AI Retention Engine cuts voluntary 22%, multi-year 68%, 140% whale NRR. Q4 stable at 2.5-2.7%.

Sarah Chen: Thank you for your insightful questions. We are confident in our ability to continue to deliver strong results and create value for our shareholders. Thank you to our employees, customers, and partners.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
